geo.label: March lift-off intact, war caps the pace
parts: Macro Stance

The first day of war delivered a textbook panic-and-reversal on Wall Street, and the close matters more than the open. Al Jazeera reported the Dow plunging more than 800 points as Russia attacked Ukraine [[n1126]], yet the S&P 500 finished at 4,288.70 index points, +1.50%, the Nasdaq 100 at 13,974.67 index points, +3.44%, and the Dow at 33,223.83 index points, +0.28% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). The reversal is consistent with investors treating the Western response so far as a manageable growth shock rather than a recession trigger, and the bid for Treasuries may be easing the case for a more aggressive Fed. We stay Mixed: the S&P 500 is still -4.16% over five sessions, and the VIX still closed at 30.32 index points after slipping only 0.70 points.
Rates & Curve

Treasuries took the haven bid at the long end while the front end kept its Fed pricing. The 2Y closed at 1.54% and the 10Y at 1.96%, leaving 10Y-2Y at +42 bps and 10Y-3M at +164 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-24). Over 20 observations the 2Y is up 41 bps from 1.13% and the 10Y up 11 bps, a bear flattening that has cut the spread by 30 bps; over the last five observations the 2Y rose 2 bps while the 10Y fell 7 bps. The curve remains positively sloped. Reuters reported Treasury yields sliding as Russia invaded [[n0241]], and a Reuters commentary argued the bond market is sending flawed signals on the US economy [[n1965]], a caution against reading the long-end rally as a clean verdict on growth.
New / Most Important

The domestic data still support March lift-off. The Real Economy Blog charted initial jobless claims continuing to decline [[n1909]], even as the Conference Board said consumer confidence declined for a second consecutive month in February [[n1906]]. The war reaches households through prices: CBS News described how the Ukraine crisis is already hitting Americans' wallets [[n1257]], and ABC7 Chicago reported President Biden promising to soften the blow from rising gasoline prices as much as he can [[n1300]]. Policy is the second channel. Al Jazeera reported Biden unveiling new Russia sanctions over the invasion [[n1281]], and Reuters quoted the White House saying all options are on the table [[n0227]]. Crude's verdict was restrained: Brent settled at 99.08 USD/bbl, +2.31% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24), after OilPrice.com reported prices soaring past $100 [[n1772]].
Playbook ✓

Action: hold a barbell of quality mega-cap technology and US energy producers, funded from consumer discretionary and banks. Trigger: keep it while the S&P 500 holds its 4,288.70 close and the 10Y stays at or below its 1.96% close. KALB's report of a Fed governor opening the door to a half-point March hike [[n1941]] is the hawkish tail; if that view gains ground, cut growth exposure and shorten duration. What changes the call: Brent settling back above the $100 mark Reuters used to chart oil's journey from worthless in the pandemic [[n0743]], which would turn the consumer energy tax from a risk into a forecast.

geo.label: Gas shock collides with ECB normalisation
parts: Macro Stance

Europe carries the war's economic incidence, and its markets closed before the US reversal. The STOXX 600 fell 3.28% to 438.96 index points, the DAX 3.96% to 14,052.10 index points and the CAC 40 3.83% to 6,521.05 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24); CNBC reported European stocks closing 3% lower as the DAX slid 4% [[n0691]]. Bloomberg called Russia's 33% equity crash the fifth-worst in market history [[n0762]]. We are Bearish because the region imports the energy shock directly.
Activity & Inflation

The pre-war signal was improving: Times of Malta reported eurozone growth jumping as virus restrictions eased [[n1059]]. Energy now overrides it. Dutch TTF gas settled at 134.32 EUR/MWh, +51.10% on the day and +92.44% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24), while Al Jazeera reported Europe's gas prices soaring 62% as the crisis put fuel supply at risk [[n1127]]. Reuters asked how dependent Germany is on Russian gas [[n1130]]. That mix lifts headline inflation while squeezing real incomes, which complicates the path Reuters reported toward an ECB deposit rate of -0.25% by year-end [[n1040]].
New / Most Important

Banks with Russian franchises took the hardest hit: Societe Generale fell 12.15% and Raiffeisen Bank International 23.14% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24), even as Reuters reported SocGen saying its Rosbank unit operates in a normal manner [[n0774]] and UniCredit saying its Russian arm is self-funded and well covered [[n0794]]. Germany suspended Hermes export credit guarantees for Russia, Reuters reported, citing Handelsblatt [[n0704]], and GOV.UK published what the Foreign Secretary called the UK's most punishing sanctions [[n1286]].
Playbook ✓

Action: underweight euro-area cyclicals and banks with eastern exposure against energy-security beneficiaries; Reuters reported European defence stocks rising as Russia invaded [[n0690]], and Rheinmetall gained 3.38% to 100.05 EUR (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). Trigger: hold while TTF stays far above 91.84 EUR/MWh, its level 20 sessions earlier. What changes the call: gas retracing most of the +51.10% jump, which would ease the stagflation squeeze and reopen the case for European cyclicals.

geo.label: Easing bias versus the regulatory discount
parts: Macro Stance

China meets the war shock with the opposite policy bias to the West, and that is the core of a Mixed stance. Reuters reported China's inflation slowing and leaving room for policy easing [[n0162]], while Bloomberg described the People's Bank seizing the moment for stimulus as the Fed hikes [[n0147]]. Against that, the private-sector growth engines remain under regulatory pressure: Bloomberg reported Alibaba planning for a new normal of low growth as the crackdown bites [[n0229]]. Beijing's diplomacy adds a third layer, with PBS reporting that China avoided criticism of the Russian attack and called for talks [[n1284]]. Easing supports onshore assets; the crackdown and sanctions-adjacent risk cap offshore valuations.
PMIs & Activity

The latest activity evidence is soft. Reuters reported January factory activity contracting as COVID lockdowns bit, according to the Caixin PMI [[n0152]], while China Daily Global Edition reported industrial profits rebounding in 2021 as production improved [[n0150]]. Profits are the backward-looking read; the PMI is the forward one, and it describes a demand-constrained economy rather than an overheating one. Autos are stable rather than strong: the Best Selling Cars Blog reported January wholesales up 0.9% in a stable market [[n0195]]. Policy-directed investment is the bright spot, with Global Times reporting China expected to add a record 75-90GW of solar capacity in 2022 [[n0214]], the kind of state-steered capex that offsets weak private demand.
Credit Impulse

Credit is where the easing bias should show first. MacroMicro's tracking of LPR interest-rate swaps [[n0154]] is the market's gauge of further loan-prime-rate cuts, and slowing inflation gives the PBOC cover to keep nudging borrowing costs lower. The risk is that credit is being offered into weak demand: the January PMI shows activity had not yet responded to earlier easing. BNP Paribas Asset Management framed US-China monetary policy divergence as a defining theme [[n1141]]. The war widens that divergence, because a Fed that tightens while the PBOC eases narrows China's rate advantage, but cheaper domestic credit is exactly what property and local investment need. We would treat a clear acceleration in new loans as the trigger to add onshore cyclicals.
Property

Property remains a drag rather than a source of systemic contagion, but the drag is still deepening. CNBC reported Moody's downgrading Shimao as debt troubles drag on [[n0238]], and The Standard reported Fantasia being sued over a bond default [[n0203]]. Forbes noted that Hong Kong tycoon Joseph Lau's fortune edged up despite an Evergrande loss [[n0219]], a reminder that developer stress is still showing up in concentrated holders' fortunes. Hong Kong adds a separate problem: Al Jazeera reported the territory unveiling a $22bn budget as zero-COVID hammers businesses [[n0220]]. The policy response visible so far is incremental, and the downgrade cycle argues it is not yet enough to stabilise developer funding.
Fiscal, Policy & Trade

The policy calendar is the near-term swing factor. The South China Morning Post previewed what to expect from China's 2022 'two sessions' as Beijing plots its course [[n0245]], where growth targets and fiscal quotas set the tone for the year. Trade is being rewired by the war: Reuters reported Russia's trade flow shifting towards China as sanctions start [[n0192]], and Global Times quoted analysts saying Ukraine tensions will affect agricultural trade but with limited impact on China [[n0242]]. The Atlantic Council described Russia and China as partners in de-dollarisation [[n0168]]. The investor risk is secondary sanctions on Chinese firms that deepen Russian commerce; Moneycontrol examined what possible trade sanctions against Russia could mean for India and China [[n0226]], and the answer depends on whether Western controls extend to third-country suppliers.
Markets & Flows

Onshore and offshore markets diverged on the first day of war. The Shanghai Composite fell 1.70% to 3,429.96 index points while the Hang Seng dropped 3.21% to 22,901.56 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). Platform stocks took the brunt in Hong Kong: Alibaba fell 6.67% to 104.90 HKD, Tencent 3.87% to 406.32 HKD and Xiaomi 5.08% to 14.96 HKD. In the later US session, which delivered the reversal, the KWEB China internet ETF rose 0.95% and the Alibaba ADR slipped only 0.72% to 108.93 USD, while ASHR fell 1.04%. The offshore discount reflects regulation as much as war: Reuters reported fresh fears over a Beijing crackdown driving a China tech rout [[n0204]], and The Japan Times reported China telling banks and state firms to report their exposure to Jack Ma's Ant [[n0194]].
New / Most Important

Alibaba's latest outlook is the day's key China datapoint. Modern Retail reported the company betting on international growth as regulatory pressure grows [[n0660]], a pivot that implies less room for growth at home. Over five sessions the Hong Kong shares are down 14.72% and the ADR 13.24% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24), so the reset met a stock that had already de-rated. Washington's pressure has not paused either: Reuters reported the US adding e-commerce sites operated by Tencent and Alibaba to its 'notorious markets' list [[n0170]], keeping a US-policy overhang on the platforms even as Western attention turns to Russia.
Playbook ✓

Action: favour onshore exposure through ASHR over offshore platform names, and keep KWEB as a tactical trade only. Trigger: a two-sessions growth target and fiscal quota that confirm the easing bias, alongside a Caixin PMI that stops contracting. What changes the call: evidence that Chinese banks or exporters face Western secondary sanctions for absorbing diverted Russian trade, which would hit onshore and offshore assets together. ⚠ Divergence: policy is easing and inflation is slowing, yet Hong Kong-listed Alibaba fell 6.67% and Xiaomi 5.08% while the Shanghai Composite lost 1.70%; the binding constraint on offshore valuations is the regulatory discount, not the cost of money.

geo.label: Imported inflation tests a patient BOJ
parts: Macro Stance

Japan is a net energy importer facing a terms-of-trade hit, which makes the war a mild stagflation shock rather than a growth opportunity. Reuters reported consumer inflation in Japan's capital perking up, with the Ukraine crisis set to add pressure [[n0989]]. The Nikkei 225 fell 1.81% to 25,970.82 index points in Thursday's session after the holiday break (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24), leaving it -5.42% over five sessions. SoftBank Group dropped 6.83% and Advantest 4.14%, while Tokyo Electron rose 1.12%. Reuters reported that a board reshuffle may open scope for a less dovish BOJ [[n1331]], but energy-driven inflation is not the demand-pull variety the central bank wants to see. Mixed.
Activity & Currency

Activity was losing momentum before the war. CNBC reported February factory activity growth falling to a five-month low [[n1337]], and The Guardian Nigeria News reported that GDP rebounded before the Omicron wave hit [[n1329]]. The dollar index rose 0.99% to 97.14 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). With the BOJ still applying negative rates, as Asahi Shimbun reported in the case of MUFG Bank deposits [[n1323]], while the US 2Y is up 41 bps over 20 observations, the widening rate gap is the channel through which imported energy costs can be amplified for Japanese households and margins. Fiscal room to cushion households is thin; Big Think noted that no country owes more than Japan relative to GDP [[n1325]]. EWJ fell only 0.58% in the US session, in a session that traded after the Tokyo close and during the US rebound.
Playbook ✓

Action: prefer semiconductor-equipment exposure such as Tokyo Electron over energy-intensive domestic cyclicals, and do not rely on the yen as a portfolio haven while the rate gap widens. Trigger: Tokyo inflation feeding into BOJ communication, given the board changes Reuters flagged. What changes the call: a rebound in the next factory survey, or a BOJ that explicitly looks through energy inflation, which would favour exporters such as Toyota, down 1.53% to 2,091.00 JPY (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24).

geo.label: RBA patience, commodity cushion
parts: Macro Stance

Australia absorbed the first-day shock through its equity market and its miners. SMH reported the Ukraine crisis wiping more than $70b off the ASX in a 'sea of red' [[n1317]]; the S&P/ASX 200 closed 2.99% lower at 6,990.60 index points, with BHP down 6.92% and Fortescue 4.18% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). The cushion is commodity exposure: higher energy and food prices raise national income even as they squeeze households. Mixed.
Demand & Financing

Household demand faces a real-income squeeze. ABC reported wages recording their worst result in seven years [[n0086]], and separately that a huge shortage of talent is pushing wages higher, but not as fast as the cost of living [[n0047]]. That is why the RBA can wait: WSJ reported the RBA's Harper backing a review and the central bank declining to follow the Fed on rate increases [[n0027]]. Grocers confirm the cost pressure, with Reuters reporting Coles flagging inflation as cost controls limited a first-half profit dip [[n0041]] and AFR reporting Woolworths cutting its dividend as lockdown costs crimped results [[n0070]]. Lenders are moving anyway; ANZ said it is lifting rates on some lending and savings accounts [[n0073]], and Banking Day reported the RBA planning floating-rate repos with shorter tenors [[n0063]]. Commonwealth Bank fell 2.05% to 94.71 AUD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24).
Playbook ✓

Action: favour energy and food-linked exporters over banks and discretionary retailers. Trigger: the ASX 200 holding 6,838.30 index points, its level 20 sessions earlier. What changes the call: an RBA pivot toward early hikes, which the WSJ report argues against, or a slide in iron ore if China follows through on the iron ore single market The Australian reported it threatening [[n0050]].

geo.label: Frontline risk premium, NBP squeezed
parts: Macro Stance

Poland is the EU's frontline economy in this war, and the market priced it as such. Bankier.pl described a crash on the Warsaw bourse and 'war panic' on the exchange [[n1536]], while Miesięcznik Finansowy BANK reported every WIG20 company falling after the Russian attack [[n1542]]. The macro problem is that the shock lands on an economy already running hot: Forsal.pl reported GUS putting January inflation at 9.2% [[n1404]], and 300Gospodarka reported Eurostat ranking Poland's 8.7% reading the fourth highest in the EU [[n1500]]. A weaker zloty imports more inflation just as growth confidence weakens, so the central bank faces a harder trade-off than its western peers. Bearish.
Markets

The sell-off was concentrated in banks and in companies with direct Ukrainian exposure. The Beta ETF WIG20TR tracker fell 10.38% to 31.50 PLN and the US-listed EPOL dropped 7.80% to 17.50 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). Banks led the decline: PKO Bank Polski fell 16.82%, Bank Pekao 14.52% and mBank 14.56%. Clothing retailer LPP collapsed 25.19% to 9,650.00 PLN, Allegro fell 13.77% and coking-coal miner JSW 13.65%. Currency stress compounded the move: Rzeczpospolita reported the zloty under pressure and at its cheapest in months [[n1571]], and Money.pl reported the currency losing ground after the Russian assault [[n1572]]. Rzeczpospolita summed up the consequences of the invasion as higher inflation and a weaker zloty [[n1556]]. The starting point was already fragile; Bankier.pl had reported the WIG20 at its lowest since May 2021 days before the invasion [[n1447]].
Fiscal & Politics

Fiscal policy was stretched before the war, and security will stretch it further. Bankier.pl reported the government adopting the draft Homeland Defence Act and asked whether NBP profits will finance the armed forces [[n1481]]; Money.pl warned that public debt will rise through the NBP and grow more costly over time [[n1422]]. Rate hikes raise that cost, as an expert explained to Business Insider Polska [[n1429]]. Money.pl reported Fitch's rating decision citing high inflation and problems with the European Commission [[n1424]]. Tax politics remain noisy: Biznes Wprost reported dismissals over the Polski Ład reform sweeping through the finance ministry [[n1439]], and Wyborcza.pl's coverage put the war, Polski Ład and the Sejm's sitting side by side [[n1564]]. A rule-of-law deal, which EUobserver reported Poland edging toward [[n1362]], would unlock EU funds and has become a larger swing factor for the fiscal path.
Corporate & Sectors

Corporate exposure to Ukraine is direct and visible. Wiadomości Handlowe reported LPP closing its Ukrainian stores and moving its office from Kyiv to Lviv [[n1555]], Retailnet.pl reported CCC closing its stores in Ukraine [[n1524]], and Bankier.pl reported Grupa Kęty halting production in Borodianka [[n1532]]. StockWatch.pl summarised listed companies limiting their Ukrainian operations amid market panic [[n1547]]. In banking, PKO BP's chief told Bankier.pl the group had prepared for all scenarios at its Ukrainian unit Kredobank [[n1546]], but Business Insider Polska reported Poles withdrawing more cash from banks, as at the start of the pandemic [[n1543]]. Energy is the policy-sensitive sector: wnp.pl reported Russian crude accounting for less than half of Orlen's refinery throughput [[n1562]], and Forsal.pl reported Orlen's chief pledging to terminate contracts with those manipulating fuel prices [[n1523]]. Orlen fell 7.68% to 62.96 PLN and PGE 8.90% to 6.57 PLN (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). Allegro adds a governance change, with Bankier.pl reporting that chief executive Francois Nuyts will step down [[n1530]].
Geopolitics & Security

The security premium is now explicit. Wiadomości Onet reported the Polish army raising its combat readiness [[n1563]] and a Russian strike on military facilities 75 km from the Polish border [[n1553]]. A Rzeczpospolita poll found 71.1% of Poles believe Russia could attack Poland [[n1557]]. Allied reinforcement is the offset: Notes From Poland reported the UK sending an advanced air-defence system to boost NATO's eastern flank [[n1382]], and Military Times reported American troops being welcomed in Poland amid tightening security [[n1379]]. Foreign Policy argued the crisis is turning Poland into a strategic player [[n1372]], and NATO's North Atlantic Council issued a statement on Russia's attack on Ukraine [[n1304]]. Energy security matters as much as troops: Reuters had reported the Yamal-Europe pipeline flowing east as the crisis escalated [[n1081]]. InfoMigrants reported European countries preparing for refugees from Ukraine [[n1371]], a humanitarian responsibility that could also carry fiscal and labour-market consequences for neighbouring states, Poland among them.
New / Most Important

The policy question is how the NBP answers a currency shock layered on top of January's inflation spike. Miesięcznik Finansowy BANK asked how the war will affect the Polish economy and decisions on rate hikes [[n1533]]. Rzeczpospolita reported that the MPC's February move lifted rates to their highest in almost nine years [[n1399]], and The Banker reported Governor Glapiński taking aim at inflation [[n1361]]. The labour market gives less cover than before: Obserwator Gospodarczy reported unemployment rising for the first time in almost a year [[n1516]], even though pb.pl had reported the average wage rising 9.6% in 2021 [[n1402]], a wage base that makes second-round inflation effects more likely. Parkiet's assessment of the attack's consequences for markets [[n1522]] bears on a choice between tightening into the shock to defend the zloty and pausing to protect growth and the banks.
Playbook ✓

Action: stay underweight Polish equities, with banks the funding leg against energy-security and defence exposure elsewhere in Europe; XTB.com's list of four defence-sector stocks [[n1519]] points to defence as a theme for local investors. Trigger: further zloty weakness and fuel-price acceleration, which Agro Profil reported will speed up after the invasion [[n1568]]. What changes the call: an NBP response that stabilises the currency, a rule-of-law settlement that releases EU funds, and evidence that cash withdrawals are not turning into deposit flight; PKO Bank Polski at 35.95 PLN and the WIG20TR tracker at 31.50 PLN are the capitulation markers. ⚠ Divergence: higher rates should help Polish bank margins, yet PKO, Pekao and mBank fell between 14.52% and 16.82%; the market is pricing Ukraine exposure, deposit behaviour and Swiss-franc mortgage risk, where INFOR.PL reported falling optimism about settlements with banks [[n1558]], above the rate tailwind.
Narrative

Technology led the reversal: XLK rose 3.42% to 152.28 USD, with Microsoft +5.11%, Nvidia +6.08% and Apple +1.67% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). Falling long yields likely did much of the work; Investopedia described investors fleeing stocks for gold and bonds [[n0800]], but the bond rally also lowered the discount rate on long-duration earnings. Over 20 sessions XLK is flat at -0.10%.
Reported

Nvidia's fourth-quarter fiscal 2022 release [[n0891]] remains the most recent mega-cap print, and Counterpoint Research reported global smartphone revenue hitting a record of about $450 billion in 2021 with Apple capturing its highest-ever share in the fourth quarter [[n0993]].
EPS Upside Watch

Cybersecurity is plausibly the cleanest earnings link to the war: CrowdStrike rose 13.01%, Palo Alto Networks 13.05% and Zscaler 10.02%. CrowdStrike's research on access brokers, their targets and their worth [[n1624]] describes the threat economy those budgets fight.
⚡ Breaking Convention

High-multiple software normally suffers in a crisis. Here the war pulled long yields lower and put cyber defence in focus at once, so Fortune's question of how low tech stocks can fall [[n0374]] has a different answer when the discount rate is falling.
Narrative

Communication services joined the rally, with XLC up 2.80% to 67.44 USD, but Meta Platforms (FB) remains the swing factor: +4.61% to 207.60 USD yet -29.54% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). Al Jazeera reported that Meta's plunge is unmatched among big tech stocks in recent years [[n0294]].
Reported

Reuters reported Facebook launching Reels globally, betting on its 'fastest growing' format [[n0444]], and Moneycontrol reported a pilot sharing ad revenues with Reels creators [[n0967]]. Reuters also reported Zuckerberg unveiling AI projects aimed at building the metaverse [[n0996]].
EPS Upside Watch

Alphabet rose 4.00%, Netflix 6.14%, Snap 5.00% and Pinterest 8.34%. Sensor Tower reported global consumer spending in the top 100 subscription apps climbing 41% to $18.3 billion in 2021 [[n1785]], support for subscription models over pure advertising if fuel prices squeeze marketing budgets.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Telecoms, the textbook defensive, lagged: AT&T fell 1.19% and Verizon 1.54%. In this war rally the market paid for growth platforms over bond-like carriers, the reverse of the standard crisis playbook.
Narrative

Financials failed to join the rebound: XLF fell 1.20% to 37.88 USD while the S&P 500 gained 1.50%. JPMorgan dropped 2.78%, Citigroup 4.03% and Bank of America 2.64% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). A curve at +42 bps that has bear-flattened over 20 observations caps the margin upside banks were promised from lift-off.
Reported

Reuters reported RBC profit rising on wealth and loan growth while flagging a mortgage slowdown [[n0137]], and the Financial Times reported Morgan Stanley disclosing twin probes into big stock transactions [[n0733]]; Morgan Stanley fell 1.86%.
EPS Upside Watch

Net interest income remains the upside lever if the Fed moves in March. A Federal Reserve note on the drivers of bank supply of business loans [[n1151]] is a reminder that business lending is one channel through which a March hike would reach bank earnings.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Rate hikes are supposed to help banks. Here sanctions compliance and counterparty risk dominate; the Association of Certified Financial Crime Specialists warned that sanctions, AML and cyber risks soar [[n0662]]. Russian exposure is an operating cost before it becomes a credit loss.
Narrative

Energy equities lagged the commodity: XLE fell 0.78% to 67.11 USD while Brent rose 2.31% to 99.08 USD/bbl and WTI 0.77% to 92.81 USD/bbl (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). Reuters reported oil topping $105 as Russia invaded [[n1774]], before crude gave back much of that spike into the settlement.
Reported

BBC reported oil hitting a seven-year high even as shares rebounded [[n0742]]. Reuters reported Chevron monitoring the Russia situation and saying it can adjust crude supply [[n0676]], while Saipem tempered its green ambitions after a loss prompted a rethink [[n1000]].
EPS Upside Watch

With Brent +10.14% over 20 sessions against XLE's +2.93%, equities price only a fraction of the strip. Exxon Mobil fell 1.26%, Chevron 0.52% and Schlumberger 3.57%, which could leave room for estimates to catch up with crude if prices hold.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Integrated majors fell on the day GMA Network reported oil rising above $105 after the attack [[n1773]]; money moved toward technology on the day while energy equities slipped. That gap between commodity and equity is an opportunity, not a warning.
Narrative

Industrials rose 1.28% to 96.82 USD, led by defence: Lockheed Martin +1.75%, Northrop Grumman +2.44%, Raytheon Technologies (RTX) +2.18% and the ITA ETF +2.75% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). Reuters reported BAE Systems saying the Russian invasion will sharpen the focus on defence [[n0665]], and Fortune reported Reddit's WallStreetBets celebrating war-friendly stocks [[n0748]].
Reported

Safran reported its full-year 2021 results [[n0140]] and, per Reuters, boosted titanium stocks to shore up its supply chain [[n0770]]. Bloomberg reported jet-engine makers looking for titanium supplies outside Russia [[n0713]].
EPS Upside Watch

Quanta Services rose 10.60%, while Caterpillar fell 1.06% and is -13.81% over 20 sessions, so the rally was selective. Deere, which Reuters said aims for bigger profit as price hikes powered an earnings beat [[n0269]], rose 1.55%.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Aerospace is not a clean war winner. Airbus fell 4.41% and Boeing has lost 9.36% over five sessions; CNN had reported airlines cancelling Ukraine flights as the threat of war grew [[n1675]]. Titanium dependence and route disruption cut against defence budgets inside the same sector.
Narrative

Consumer discretionary bounced 2.29% to 172.77 USD on Amazon +4.51% and Tesla +4.81%, but is -7.16% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). Fuel is the war's main channel to households, and The Conversation warned of higher food and gas prices and an increased risk of recession [[n1123]].
Reported

The Business of Fashion reported TJX results missing estimates due to Omicron store closures [[n0627]]; Bloomberg reported eBay warning it is still losing customers [[n0568]]; Retail Dive reported Wayfair's revenue falling 11.4% in the fourth quarter as losses widened [[n1783]].
EPS Upside Watch

Home improvement is holding up: Reuters reported Lowe's optimistic on demand despite rising interest rates [[n0973]]. Auto Remarketing reported KAR selling its ADESA US physical auction business to Carvana for $2.2B [[n0789]]; Carvana rose 10.91%. The Verge reported Etsy hitting sellers with a 30 percent transaction-fee increase [[n0689]], a platform testing its pricing power.
⚡ Breaking Convention
The rebound was led by mega-cap platforms, not by the household. With confidence falling and fuel prices rising, discretionary spending faces a tax that the index rally ignored.
Narrative

Staples were a funding leg: XLP fell 1.72% to 73.54 USD while the S&P 500 rose, with Procter & Gamble -2.69%, Coca-Cola -1.75% and PepsiCo -1.74% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). Investors sold defensives to buy beta, a rotation that works only if the energy shock stays contained; Walmart slipped 0.39%.
Reported

Reuters reported Coca-Cola HBC readying Russia contingencies as profits rose [[n0467]] and then shutting its Ukraine plant [[n0670]]. Reuters also reported Nestle temporarily closing factories and warehouses in Ukraine [[n0735]]; Nestle fell 3.15% to 115.16 CHF.
EPS Upside Watch

Pricing power is the swing factor. CBC reported more shoppers feeling inflation pressure and turning to dollar stores for deals [[n0732]], while Costco rose 2.08%, a sign that value formats can take share as budgets tighten. CSP Daily News reported private labels lifting US sales to $199 billion in 2021 [[n1887]], a structural base for trading down.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Staples usually outperform in war. They fell as money rotated toward beta, and rising input costs threaten margins faster than prices can follow: wheat rose 5.71% to 926.00 US cents/bu and corn 1.65% to 695.00 US cents/bu (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24).
Narrative

Health care rose only 0.40% to 127.06 USD, a laggard in the rebound, with Pfizer -1.94%, Johnson & Johnson -1.91% and Merck -3.07% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). The defensive bid never arrived because investors chose growth beta.
Reported

Moderna was the standout: WSJ reported it beating profit estimates on Covid-19 vaccine sales [[n0727]], and the stock rose 15.10% to 156.23 USD. BioPharma Dive reported Moderna betting on booster demand and advancing a new bivalent shot [[n0728]].
EPS Upside Watch

Managed care carries deal risk: Reuters reported the US suing to block UnitedHealth's $8 bln deal for Change Healthcare [[n0787]], and UnitedHealth fell 0.81%. Biotech rallied, with XBI up 4.58%, and Eli Lilly rose 2.00%. Fierce Biotech reported Baxter reaching an $18M settlement with the SEC over allegedly inflating income [[n1754]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

Health care's haven status failed on a war day. The sector's value now lies in idiosyncratic catalysts such as vaccine contracts and pipeline news, not in defensive flows; Fierce Pharma's report that analysts expect Eylea to 'remain king' [[n0749]] shows franchise durability still earns a premium.
Narrative

Materials split between farm inputs and metals: XLB slipped 0.29% to 81.37 USD, but CF Industries rose 5.48%, Nutrien 3.16% and Mosaic 0.33% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). Bloomberg reported fertilizer shortages from Russia-Ukraine tension may hit the US growing season [[n0578]].
Reported

Reuters reported MP Materials posting higher profit as rare earth prices surge [[n0720]], while the shares rose 7.37% in the session. The Financial Post reported Agnico Eagle announcing the surprise exit of its CEO amid an earnings miss [[n0658]].
EPS Upside Watch

Aluminium rose 3.34% to 3,457.50 USD/t and palladium 2.48% to 2,498.60 USD/oz. Reuters reported oil, gas, grains and metals spiking as Russia invaded [[n1774]]; markets can attach a supply-risk premium to metals with Russian sourcing.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Yahoo Finance UK reported gold hitting a one-year high as investors flocked to a safe haven [[n0706]], with futures closing at 1,926.30 USD/oz, yet GDX fell 1.93%. Newmont fell 2.24%. Miners failed to track bullion on the day, a gap that cost discipline can close, while Freeport-McMoRan rose 2.97% even as copper slipped 0.61% to 4.45 USD/lb.
Narrative

Real estate rose 1.73% to 44.74 USD as long yields eased, but is -2.91% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). A lower 10Y helps REIT valuations; rising mortgage rates work against housing turnover.
Reported

MONEY reported mortgage rates rising again on February 24 [[n1919]], and Reuters reported US existing home sales accelerating as investors elbow out first-time buyers [[n1873]]. Bloomberg reported Wall Street buying starter homes to quietly become America's landlord [[n0173]], a structural bid for single-family rental.
EPS Upside Watch

Consolidation continues in niche formats: Business Wire reported SmartStop Self Storage REIT agreeing to acquire a Strategic Storage Growth Trust II portfolio in a $280 million transaction [[n0773]], and Affordable Housing Finance reported Blackstone Real Estate launching an affordable-housing company [[n0669]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

Property rallied on a war day because the shock cut long yields while high-yield credit held up; HYG gained 0.71% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). Financing conditions did not tighten, which is why rate-sensitive real estate behaved like a bond proxy rather than a cyclical.
Narrative

Utilities rose 0.80% to 65.55 USD, led by NextEra Energy +4.31% while Duke Energy fell 0.65% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). Vistra rose 4.18% and Southern Company 0.06%. Clean-energy equipment led harder still, with Enphase Energy +16.43% and SolarEdge Technologies +14.86%.
Reported

Uniper reported achieving its 2021 financial targets and significantly reducing economic net debt [[n0980]]. Reuters reported EDF getting $2 bln of state help over nuclear-plant outages [[n0277]], a reminder of how exposed European generators are to supply shocks.
EPS Upside Watch

Energy security now reinforces decarbonisation spending. Offshore Wind reported TenneT starting a tender for 2 GW of German offshore grid connections [[n1116]], the kind of grid build that supports regulated asset growth. Enverus examined how ORDC changes are affecting ERCOT volatility [[n0131]], a reminder that merchant power earnings are tied to scarcity pricing.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Utilities are meant to be the calm corner. With TTF at 134.32 EUR/MWh, gas-dependent European generators face margin strain, while renewables gain an energy-security argument on top of the climate one.
Narrative

European autos were among the worst-hit groups: the SXAP tracker fell 6.09% to 57.08 EUR, BMW 7.24%, Mercedes-Benz Group 6.50%, Volkswagen preference shares 5.87% and Renault 9.07% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). NBC News reported the Ukraine crisis could create more woes for the auto industry [[n0979]].
Reported
Barron's reported Stellantis stock soaring as it posted a strong debut yearly profit [[n0622]], and Reuters reported scarcity and software set to power Mercedes-Benz through 2022 [[n0771]].
EPS Upside Watch

Scarcity pricing has supported margins, but supply is breaking again: BBC reported the Mini Oxford plant halted by the chip shortage [[n1739]]. Reuters reported Volkswagen and its top shareholder striking a framework deal for a Porsche IPO [[n0797]], a potential value catalyst, and Mercedes-Benz targeting the US for hands-free driving certification this year [[n0725]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

Scarcity protects margins only while plants can build. A war that adds component and energy disruption converts the 2021 pricing tailwind into lost volume, which is why strong 2021 profits failed to protect the shares.
Narrative

US semiconductors rallied while Asia's fell: SOXX rose 3.66% to 469.24 USD and ASML's US line 3.97%, but the TSMC ADR fell 3.47%, SK Hynix 6.84% and Samsung Electronics 3.77% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). Asian sessions closed before the US reversal, and TSMC's US line still fell after it.
Reported

The Economist Intelligence Unit reported chip makers increasing investment for 2022 amid the shortage [[n1755]], and TechCrunch reported Bosch investing $296M to produce semiconductors to combat the shortage [[n1715]].
EPS Upside Watch

Barron's listed 15 chip stocks it called real bargains that keep getting cheaper [[n0652]]. TechSpot reported that Nvidia had reportedly spent $10 billion for a chunk of TSMC's 5nm capacity [[n1681]], evidence of prepaid demand. Intel rose 4.64% and AMD 6.24%, after Yahoo Finance reported AMD now worth more than rival Intel [[n0534]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

Sanctions normally read as a revenue threat for chipmakers. The split mainly reflects timing, since Asian sessions closed before the US reversal; it still favours US designers over Asian memory makers while energy costs and supply-chain risk weigh on the Asian names.

earnings_pattern.title: War-Week Results: Pricing Power Rewarded, Pandemic Volume Punished
parts: Rewarded

Moderna rose 15.10% to 156.23 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24) after CNBC reported it expects at least $19 billion in Covid vaccine sales in 2022 and posted a big fourth-quarter earnings beat [[n0729]]. Barron's reported Stellantis stock soaring as the Dodge and Jeep maker posted a strong debut yearly profit [[n0622]], and CNBC reported Nikola shares surging on an earnings beat and plans to generate revenue in 2022 [[n0772]]. Earlier in the season, Reuters reported Deere aiming for bigger profit as price hikes powered an earnings beat [[n0269]], a beat powered by pricing rather than volume.
Punished

The Financial Times reported Rolls-Royce shares tumbling after it said chief Warren East is leaving [[n0755]], and The Guardian put the lost share value at £1.5bn [[n0753]]. Bloomberg reported eBay warning it is still losing customers as its shares fell [[n0568]]. Reuters reported Home Depot's margin warning casting a shadow on a solid quarter [[n0943]], and CNBC reported Roblox shares closing down 26% after an earnings miss [[n0893]].
Pattern

Results that change the macro narrative get priced; results that confirm demand normalisation get sold. Companies with scarcity or pricing power, from vaccines to trucks, autos and farm equipment, were rewarded, while platforms reliant on pandemic-era volume faced guidance scepticism. CNBC reported Coinbase posting a big revenue beat but expecting trading volume to fall in the first quarter [[n0679]], a beat whose forward question, trading volume, the market still has to price. Leadership changes compounded misses wherever investors were already doubting execution.
Attention into EPS

Energy, fertilizer and defence are where 2022 estimates look most exposed to upward revision, because the commodity moves likely arrived after many forecasts were set: Brent is +10.14% and wheat +16.48% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). Consumer discretionary carries the mirror-image downside from fuel. Wayfair's revenue fall, reported by Retail Dive [[n1783]], shows pandemic-era volume normalising.
Playbook

Buy post-results weakness in companies whose guidance rests on price rather than volume, and fade beats that depend on pandemic-era activity. Lowe's optimism on demand despite rising rates, reported by Reuters [[n0973]], is the template for resilient guidance. What changes the call: a broad demand slowdown that erodes pricing power too, visible first in retailer comparable sales and in fertilizer and energy companies cutting volume guidance.

underowned.title: Fertilizer and Farm Inputs: The Food-Security Trade
parts: Attention Gap

Markets fixated on oil and gas, but grain and fertilizer carry equally direct Russia-Ukraine exposure. CNBC described how an invasion of Ukraine, the 'breadbasket of Europe', could hit supply chains [[n1732]], and wheat rose 5.71% to 926.00 US cents/bu, +18.64% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24).
Exposure & Risk

CF Industries at 78.56 USD (+5.48%), Nutrien at 77.48 USD (+3.16%) and Mosaic at 45.35 USD (+0.33%) are the listed expressions. The risk is demand destruction if farmers cut application at high prices, and political pressure if food inflation becomes the story.
Trigger to Watch
Farm Progress reported the USDA cutting corn and raising soy and wheat acreage for 2022 [[n1782]]; shifting acreage changes nutrient demand. Watch corn at 695.00 US cents/bu as the input-cost signal.

underowned.title: Cybersecurity: The War Budget Nobody Has to Approve
parts: Attention Gap

Cyber stocks led the rebound but are still priced as high-multiple software rather than security infrastructure. Niebezpiecznik published advice on the war's cybersecurity implications for Poland [[n1573]], Gazeta Prawna reported the Polish prime minister raising the cyber alert level [[n1444]], and CrowdStrike's own research mapped what access brokers target [[n1624]].
Exposure & Risk

CrowdStrike at 182.88 USD (+13.01%), Palo Alto Networks at 539.94 USD (+13.05%) and Zscaler at 263.38 USD (+10.02%) (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). All three remain long-duration equities, so valuation is the risk if yields resume their climb and the bid fades with the headlines.
Trigger to Watch

Data Center Knowledge reported Cloudflare agreeing to buy Area 1 Security to protect against phishing emails [[n0677]]; Cloudflare rose 18.66%. Further consolidation or new government procurement would confirm that budgets, not just sentiment, are moving.

underowned.title: Critical Minerals: Supply Chains Under Sanction Risk
parts: Attention Gap

The USGS released its 2022 list of critical minerals [[n1955]], and sanctions-driven rerouting raises the value of non-Russian supply. Macau Business reported nickel prices soaring on Russia tension and tight supply [[n1680]], and Trade Data Monitor described Ukraine as more than a breadbasket: a key iron ore and metals supplier [[n0052]].
Exposure & Risk

MP Materials at 43.85 USD (+7.37%) and Lynas Rare Earths at 8.95 AUD (-2.08%) (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24); palladium is +10.15% over five sessions and aluminium +12.33% over 20. Price volatility, processing bottlenecks and Chinese pricing power are the core risks.
Trigger to Watch
Watch whether aerospace and auto buyers formalise non-Russian sourcing; Bloomberg's report on jet-engine makers looking for titanium outside Russia [[n0713]] is the template for other metals.

underowned.title: Gold Miners: Bullion's Rally Without the Leverage
parts: Attention Gap

Mining.com reported the gold price blasting to a 15-month peak as war returned to Europe [[n1761]], Reuters reported gold ETFs seeing big inflows [[n1164]], and CME Group asked whether gold is about to break out of a narrow trading range [[n1970]]. Yet GDX fell 1.93% to 34.07 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24), even though it is +11.23% over 20 sessions.
Exposure & Risk

Newmont at 66.72 USD (-2.24%) reported 2021 reserves of 93 million gold ounces [[n0738]]; cost inflation from energy is the main threat to margins. Over 20 sessions GDX's +11.23% against gold's +5.28% shows the leverage does work on longer windows.
Trigger to Watch
Agnico Eagle's CEO exit amid an earnings miss [[n0658]] shows execution risk. Watch miners' cost guidance while bullion holds above 1,829.70 USD/oz, its level 20 sessions earlier.

crypto.title: Crypto Fails the Haven Test, Then Rebounds With Tech
parts: Market Context

Bitcoin closed the UTC day at 38,332.61 USD, +2.78%, but -7.63% over 20 sessions; Ether at 2,598.07 USD, +0.30% and -12.92%; Solana at 89.19 USD, +5.06% (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-24). Earlier in the day Reuters reported cryptocurrencies falling after Russia invaded [[n0863]], and Yahoo Finance UK said bitcoin crashed as claims of a safe haven were blown to bits [[n0860]]. CBS News reported cryptocurrency prices plunging as the Ukraine crisis intensified [[n0864]]. The recovery tracked the Nasdaq 100's +3.44% session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24), not gold's haven bid, and it was uneven: Dogecoin fell 3.15% to 0.12 USD and XRP slipped 0.35% to 0.70 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-24). In the US session GBTC rose 3.75% and the futures-based BITO 1.91% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24).
New / Most Important

CNBC argued the case for bitcoin as 'digital gold' is falling apart [[n0854]], and Fortune reported Putin's invasion jolting the crypto markets [[n0873]]. Euronews reported Ethereum founder Vitalik Buterin condemning the invasion as 'a crime' [[n0876]]. Bloomberg reported Coinbase saying revenue topped estimates while cautioning on trading volume [[n0678]]; the session close of 179.56 USD, +3.95% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24), may not yet reflect that report. Miners rebounded harder: Marathon Digital rose 9.13% and Riot Blockchain (RIOT) 7.83%. Bloomberg also reported one of the biggest crypto traders tapping DeFi loans for funding [[n0872]], a sign of how traders fund positions without selling, and had reported Buterin saying crypto 'welcomes' another winter [[n0815]].
Playbook

Action: treat bitcoin as high-beta Nasdaq exposure, not a war hedge, and size it alongside growth equities rather than gold; MicroStrategy's 8.75% gain shows equity proxies amplifying the coin's moves. Trigger: a daily close back above 41,500.88 USD, its level 20 sessions earlier, would confirm the risk-on recovery. What changes the call: bitcoin rising while the Nasdaq falls, which would revive the haven case, or the trading-volume decline Coinbase flagged deepening, which would hit exchange-linked equities first.

flows.title: Liquidity Holds as the Dollar and Gold Take the Haven Bid
parts: Global Liquidity

Global liquidity is still tightening along a pre-set path, and the war has not changed that yet. TD Economics argued quantitative tightening will slow deposit growth and put modest upward pressure on yields [[n0136]], and Capital Economics said it is time to talk about QT [[n1062]]. Other central banks keep moving: RNZ reported the Reserve Bank of New Zealand raising its Official Cash Rate by a quarter point to 1 percent [[n0064]], and Reuters said economists see a Bank of Canada March hike as a done deal [[n0125]], while CNBC reported South Korea's central bank holding after back-to-back hikes [[n1962]]. The RBA is also reshaping its plumbing, setting out changes to its open market operations [[n0049]]. Reuters reported the IIF saying emerging markets drove global debt to a record $303 trillion [[n1158]], a large refinancing base meeting a firmer dollar.
Rates & Dollar

The 10Y closed at 1.96% and the 2Y at 1.54% (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-24), with the curve positively sloped at +42 bps and the 20-observation move a bear flattening. The five-observation change shows the haven bid concentrated at the long end, with the 10Y down 7 bps. IEF rose 0.24% and TLT 0.07%, while SHY gained only 0.08% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). The DXY rose 0.99% to 97.14 index points; Reuters reported the dollar jumping to a near two-year high as Russia invaded [[n1125]], and the close shows that haven bid surviving the equity recovery. Topdown Charts, via Christophe Barraud, said the rise in bond yields looks like an exhausted MOVE [[n1973]], consistent with volatility in rates peaking before equities. Reuters had reported eurodollar futures betting that a hawkish Fed could ease rates slightly in 2024 [[n1051]], so the market already prices a short cycle.
Credit Check

Credit did not crack. HYG rose 0.71% to 83.14 USD and LQD 0.47% to 122.98 USD, but EMB fell 1.01% to 98.98 USD and is -5.27% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). Emerging-market dollar debt is where the war is priced: Reuters had reported Russian bonds hammered as the rouble plummeted [[n1267]], and then the rouble heading to a record low as the sell-off hit stocks [[n1775]]. Primary markets stayed open for quality issuers, with RBC Capital Markets reporting Ford breaking the green-bond record [[n1159]], and private credit is still raising money: Reuters reported Quantum Energy offering a $2.25 bln debt fund [[n0685]]. Moody's downgrade of Shimao, reported by CNBC [[n0238]], and the bond-default suit against Fantasia reported by The Standard [[n0203]] keep Chinese high yield the weak link.
Equity & Fund Flows

Measured flows point to a haven rotation, not liquidation. Reuters reported gold ETFs seeing big inflows on rising geopolitical concerns [[n1164]], and the Financial Times had reported ETF investors piling into Russian equities and defence stocks [[n0843]], a bet the Russian leg has now punished: Bloomberg reported Russian stocks slumping the most on record, erasing $150 billion in value [[n0761]], and Russian billionaires losing $39 billion in a day [[n0759]]. Leverage had already been cut; Wolf Street reported margin debt plunging as stocks tumbled while noting leverage is still gigantic [[n1139]]. Issuance is stalling at the margin, with Riviera reporting deteriorating conditions forcing Fred Olsen Windcarrier to put its IPO on hold [[n1146]]. Volkswagen said it would start a review of a Porsche AG IPO [[n0796]], a test of whether the European window stays open.
Portfolio Implication

The flow picture supports holding duration and gold as portfolio insurance while keeping equity beta concentrated in US quality growth. Emerging-market debt and European banks are where stress accumulates; the gain in HYG argues against a broad high-yield hedge. Oil importers are the second-round risk, as Reuters showed in reporting Indian shares and the rupee plunging as Russia attacked [[n1291]], and Business Today reported investors losing Rs 13 lakh crore in that crash [[n1646]]. What changes this: a renewed rise in the 2Y that outpaces the 10Y, signalling the Fed reasserting itself over the haven trade, or EMB extending its 20-session loss as Russian contagion spreads into other frontier credits.

anticipatory.title: March FOMC: Lift-Off Size Versus War Caution
parts: What Is Priced

The front end still prices lift-off: the 2Y at 1.54% is up 41 bps over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-24). Reuters reported the Fed is expected to raise rates 25 bps in March but that calls for 50 bps are growing louder [[n1857]]; China Daily reported the New York Fed president seeing no need for a 'big' rate hike in March [[n1938]], while Al Jazeera reported a Fed official leaving the door open to a half-point move [[n1878]].
Conditional Expression

If the Fed confirms a quarter-point move and cites war uncertainty, the 10Y-2Y spread at +42 bps can re-steepen and growth equities extend the reversal; express via QQQ at 340.49 USD against XLF (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). If a half-point hike stays live because energy inflation broadens, prefer SHY over TLT.
Risk

Reuters reported the January meeting readout showing the Fed not wed to a particular pace of rate hikes [[n1936]], so communication can swing either way; an oil spike that lifts inflation expectations would revive the larger move even as growth slows.

anticipatory.title: State of the Union and the US Energy Response
parts: What Is Priced

THIRTEEN listed President Biden's State of the Union address for March 1 [[n0141]]. Reuters quoted Biden saying 'Putin chose this war' [[n1277]], yet markets price a measured sanctions path: Brent closed at 99.08 USD/bbl and WTI at 92.81 USD/bbl (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24) after OilPrice.com reported prices soaring past $100 [[n1772]]. The equity reversal assumes energy flows continue.
Conditional Expression

If the address pairs tougher sanctions with gasoline relief, which ABC7 Chicago reported Biden promising [[n1300]], long XLE against XLY works as a hedge on energy escalation; if it prioritises energy-market calm, crude can retrace and consumer names recover. Exxon Mobil at 75.80 USD is the liquid single-name proxy for the first branch.
Risk

Time asked what Biden's sanctions on Russia will actually do [[n1314]], and PBS listed the steps the US has taken so far [[n1134]]; escalation into energy flows would break the premise of the equity reversal. Domestic politics cut both ways, with the Orange County Register reporting the Russia conflict separating GOP traditionalists from newcomers [[n0139]].

anticipatory.title: Europe's Gas Exit Strategy and the Summer Refill
parts: What Is Priced

TTF at 134.32 EUR/MWh, +51.10%, prices supply disruption (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). The Washington Post reported the EU will unveil a strategy to break free from Russian gas [[n1285]], and Reuters reported storage surviving winter while summer refilling looms [[n1052]]. OSW described a dangerous dependence on Russia in Germany's gas crisis [[n1093]].
Conditional Expression

A credible LNG and storage plan would cap TTF and favour European cyclicals. The EIA noted three countries provided almost 70% of the LNG Europe received in 2021 [[n1085]], which concentrates supplier risk. Expression: long Shell at 1,952.80 GBp (+0.49%) against European autos; the trade also works if the strategy disappoints, because Shell gains from higher gas while autos lose.
Risk

IEEFA asked whether the EU has diversity of supply or merely diversity of routes [[n1380]]; any interruption to Russian flows through Ukraine would overwhelm a strategy that takes years to build. The Guardian asked how Russia's assault will affect UK gas supplies [[n1381]], a reminder that contagion runs across the whole European grid.

anticipatory.title: China's Two Sessions: Stimulus Scale Versus Crackdown
parts: What Is Priced

The South China Morning Post previewed what to expect from China's 2022 'two sessions' [[n0245]]. The Shanghai Composite at 3,429.96 index points, -3.52% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24), prices moderate support, not a large package, even though Reuters reported slowing inflation leaving room for policy easing [[n0162]].
Conditional Expression

A growth target backed by fiscal quotas and infrastructure favours ASHR and materials; a cautious target keeps pressure on FXI at 35.05 USD. The South China Morning Post's report of a rust-belt province unveiling a population plan as it faces economic decline [[n0218]] points to regional demand for support, and Global Times' projected record solar additions [[n0214]] show where state-directed capex is going.
Risk

Regulation remains the swing: WSJ reported Chinese tutoring companies taking a big financial hit amid the crackdown [[n0197]], and Business Insider reported a live-streaming influencer fined $10 million for tax evasion [[n0193]], showing enforcement continuing alongside easing. The Japan Times' report on banks reporting exposure to Ant [[n0194]] keeps fintech in the regulatory frame.

catalysts.title: Moderna (MRNA)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

BioSpace reported Moderna projecting COVID-19 vaccine sales of $19 billion for 2022 [[n0997]], and Newsweek reported $12 billion in 2021 profit fuelled by vaccine sales [[n0731]]. Visible 2022 revenue funds the pipeline while booster demand settles.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The shares jumped 15.10% to 156.23 USD but are only +0.82% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). Fierce Biotech reported Merck cutting ties to Moderna's early-phase KRAS vaccine [[n0726]], a pipeline-credibility risk.
Trade Expression

Buy pullbacks that hold above 154.96 USD, the level 20 sessions earlier; exit if 2022 sales visibility is questioned. Pair against Pfizer, down 1.94% and -13.30% over 20 sessions, to isolate Moderna's guidance surprise.

catalysts.title: Alibaba (BABA)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Bloomberg reported Alibaba planning for a new normal of low growth as the crackdown bites [[n0229]]. Modern Retail reported the company betting on international growth as regulatory pressure grows [[n0660]]. Low growth plus regulatory risk caps the multiple even after the de-rating.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The ADR closed at 108.93 USD, -0.72%, and is -13.24% over five sessions; the Hong Kong line fell 6.67% to 104.90 HKD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). BBC reported Alibaba and Tencent sites added to the US 'Notorious Markets List' [[n0165]], a lingering policy overhang.
Trade Expression
Stay underweight; reassess only if the ADR reclaims 113.37 USD, its level 20 sessions earlier, on evidence of regulatory easing.

catalysts.title: Coinbase Global (COIN)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

CNBC reported Coinbase posting a big revenue beat but expecting trading volume to fall in the first quarter [[n0679]]. The thesis rests on crypto activity, which the invasion showed is tied to risk appetite rather than haven demand.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The stock closed at 179.56 USD, +3.95%, but is -13.66% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). Business Insider reported Coinbase backpedalling over its Super Bowl ad controversy [[n0116]], a marketing spend under scrutiny as volume cools.
Trade Expression

Trade it as bitcoin beta: add only on a bitcoin close above 41,500.88 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-24), and cut if guided volume weakness deepens into the next quarterly update.

catalysts.title: Rheinmetall (RHM.DE)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

BAE Systems published its 2021 full-year results [[n0653]] as Reuters reported European defence stocks rising on the invasion [[n0690]], and Business Live reported the missile maker owned by BAE Systems, Airbus and Leonardo creating 600 UK jobs [[n0603]]. The investment case is that European rearmament moves from rhetoric to orders.
Price Hurdle & Risk
Rheinmetall rose 3.38% to 100.05 EUR and is +7.51% over 20 sessions, while the DAX fell 3.96% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). The risk is that budget pledges lag the rhetoric.
Trade Expression

Hold long against the DAX; add on dips toward 93.06 EUR, its level 20 sessions earlier, and cut if governments fail to back words with budgets. US primes such as Lockheed Martin, up 1.75%, offer a lower-beta complement.

catalysts.title: Tesla (TSLA)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Reuters reported Tesla planning a new Shanghai plant to more than double China capacity [[n1760]], while WSJ reported the SEC probing trading by Elon Musk and his brother after the CEO's sales [[n0694]]. Bloomberg also reported the SEC probing Tesla stock sales by Musk and his brother Kimbal [[n0766]]. Capacity growth meets a governance overhang.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The shares rose 4.81% to 800.77 USD but are -14.58% over 20 sessions from 937.41 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). An escalating probe or a China demand slowdown are the key risks; the five-session loss of 13.28% shows how quickly sentiment can turn.
Trade Expression
Stay neutral; buy a reclaim of 937.41 USD on capacity confirmation, and cut on any escalation of the SEC matter.

catalysts.title: Chevron (CVX)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Reuters reported Chevron monitoring the Russia situation and saying it can adjust crude supply [[n0676]], and described oil's journey from worthless in the pandemic to $100 a barrel [[n0743]]. A producer that can flex supply captures the price signal directly, and BBC's report of oil at a seven-year high [[n0742]] shows the price backdrop.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Chevron fell 0.52% to 134.85 USD and is +1.63% over 20 sessions, against Brent's +10.14% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). Exxon Mobil fell 1.26% and ConocoPhillips 0.57%, so the whole group lagged crude. A crude retracement on diplomacy is the main risk.
Trade Expression
Buy the equity-commodity gap, paired against XLY to hedge the consumer energy tax; stop out if Brent loses 89.96 USD/bbl, its level 20 sessions earlier.

retail_intro: On the first day of the war the dominant crowd narrative is the war trade, defence contractors as the one bet that wins whatever comes next, running alongside the familiar mechanism of selling the outbreak and buying once the worst case is on the screen, which delivered a same-day rebound in US shares [[n0742]].

retail.title: Aerospace & Defense ETF / ITA — the war trade gets its Reddit moment
parts: Why Retail Is Here

The crowd's story is blunt: war has returned to Europe [[n1761]], governments will spend on weapons, and the companies that build them win whatever happens next. On the day Russia invaded Ukraine [[n1262]], that story printed in green. The ITA aerospace and defence fund rose 2.75% to $104.49, Northrop Grumman gained 2.44% to $395.49, Raytheon Technologies 2.18% and Lockheed Martin 1.75% to $395.71, while Rheinmetall climbed 3.38% to €100.05 on a day the DAX fell 3.96% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). The emotional pull is certainty in chaos: when every other screen is red, a contractor whose customer is a government feels like the closest thing to a sure thing. It is an uncomfortable trade to cheer, which has not stopped the cheering [[n0748]].
What Is Driving It

The catalyst is the invasion and the policy response it forces. Reuters reports European defence stocks rising as Russia invades [[n0690]], and Washington and London answered with sanctions, Biden unveiling a new package [[n1281]] and Britain imposing what its Foreign Secretary calls the UK's most punishing sanctions [[n1286]]. The cross-asset tape shows why defence stood out. Reuters had oil topping $105 with gas, grains and metals spiking as Russia invaded [[n1774]], before Brent settled 2.31% higher at $99.08 a barrel; the STOXX 600 lost 3.28% and the FTSE 100 3.88%, while the S&P 500 finished up 1.50% at 4,288.70 index points and the Nasdaq 100 up 3.44% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). In Europe, where the selling was worst, Rheinmetall rose against the tape; in New York, the contractors rose with it.
The Social Signal

This time the attention is on the record. Fortune reports Reddit's WallStreetBets celebrating war-friendly stocks as the Nasdaq and S&P made huge rebounds [[n0748]]: the forum that made its name on short squeezes is now trading a geopolitical theme. The funnel is visible too: Masterworks is publishing a guide to the five largest publicly traded defence contractors [[n0781]], and a day before the invasion the Financial Times reported ETF investors piling into Russian equities and defence stocks [[n0843]]. Robinhood rose 5.99% to $11.51 and GameStop 8.45% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24), a sign the retail complex was back in risk-on mode by the close. The pattern implies defence is no longer a hedge held quietly; it is a ticker the crowd brags about.
Historical Analog

The cautionary tale arrived in the same session, on the other side of the same trade. Russian stocks crashed 33% and the ruble plunged to a record low [[n0763]]; Bloomberg ranks the 33% crash as the fifth-worst in market history [[n0762]], erasing $150 billion in value [[n0761]]. Anyone who followed the reported flows into both Russian equities and defence owned a pair that split violently, one leg gutted and the other higher. The mechanism matters for the surviving leg. War premiums tend to be paid up front on expectations of bigger budgets, while contracts and revenue arrive over years, so prices can run far ahead of anything a quarterly report can confirm.
Smart Money View

The industry and the money are telling different stories. BAE Systems says the invasion will sharpen the focus on defence [[n0665]], the bull case in management's own words. Much of the haven bid went elsewhere: Investopedia describes investors fleeing stocks for the refuge of gold and bonds [[n0800]], Reuters reports big inflows into gold ETFs on rising geopolitical concerns [[n1164]], and the 10Y yield sits at 1.96%, 7 bps lower over five observations, with the 2Y at 1.54% (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-24). Even that trade comes with a caution, CNBC suggesting buyers may want to resist the rush into gold [[n1644]]. JPMorgan's Natasha Kaneva has been walking CNBC viewers through how sanctions feed into commodities [[n0644]], the channel that decides what contractors pay for inputs. The scoreboard is modest: ITA is still down 2.32% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24), bounced rather than re-rated.
When the Narrative Breaks

The war trade breaks on the same news that would relieve everyone else: a ceasefire or negotiated pause would drain the premium before any new budget is passed. It also breaks if the tech rebound keeps running, because money that came into defence as a hiding place can leave as fast as it arrived. The level to watch is ITA's $100.77 close of twenty sessions earlier: a slide back below it would say the invasion premium is gone (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). Sanctions are the wild card. The White House says all options are on the table [[n0227]], and Reuters reports Safran boosting its titanium stocks to shore up its supply chain [[n0770]], a reminder that measures which push up metal inputs raise costs for the same contractors the crowd is buying.

retail.title: 3x Nasdaq 100 ETF / TQQQ — the invasion dip, bought the same day
parts: Why Retail Is Here

The leveraged dip-buy got its answer inside one session. Al Jazeera had the Dow plunging more than 800 points as Russia attacked [[n1126]], yet it closed 0.28% higher, and TQQQ jumped 9.79% to $49.56 as the Nasdaq 100 rose 3.44% to 13,974.67 index points, with ARKK up 7.79% and AMC up 12.40% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). A session that opened in panic closed with the Nasdaq 100 up 3.44%, exactly the reversal the dip-buying crowd waits for. For dip-buyers it is vindication, the kind that tends to encourage a bigger bet next time.
Where It Breaks

One green day does not repair a bruising week. TQQQ is still down 13.49% over five sessions, and the VIX at 30.32 is only 0.70 points lower, nowhere near calm (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). The rebound came on a day of fresh sanctions, not a resolution, and the daily leverage that amplified the bounce will amplify the next drop.

retail.title: Tesla / TSLA — the SEC turns to Musk's own selling
parts: Why Retail Is Here

Tesla is the crowd's longest-running faith trade, and the regulator story has moved from Musk's complaints to Musk's own trades. The Wall Street Journal reports the SEC is probing trading by Elon Musk and his brother in the wake of the chief executive's share sales [[n0694]]; the shares, swept up in the Nasdaq rebound, rose 4.81% to $800.77 on the session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). Believers have a counter-headline: Reuters, citing sources, reports Tesla plans a new Shanghai plant to more than double its China capacity [[n1760]]. For the faithful, regulators are noise and capacity is destiny.
Where It Breaks

The bounce rode a Nasdaq rebound, not a verdict. The Guardian describes the probe as an investigation into alleged insider trading [[n0687]], a question no capacity headline answers. The shares are still down 13.28% over five sessions and 14.58% over twenty, from $937.41 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24), and YourStory counts more than $140B lost from Musk's fortune in four months [[n1643]], so the wealth effect runs both ways. The tell is relative: if Tesla gives back its 4.81% while the Nasdaq holds, the probe, not the market, is setting the price.

retail.title: Coinbase Global / COIN — the crypto broker warns its crowd is cooling
parts: Why Retail Is Here

Coinbase is how much of the crypto crowd buys, so its results double as a census. The quarter impressed, with CNBC reporting a big revenue beat [[n0679]], but Bloomberg's headline pairs the beat with a caution on trading volume [[n0678]]. The shares had closed up 3.95% at $179.56 in the regular session, still down 13.66% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-24). Bitcoin ended the UTC day 2.78% higher at $38,332.61 (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-24) after a slide that Yahoo Finance UK said blew its safe-haven claims to bits [[n0860]].
Where It Breaks

The bull case says a volatile war tape brings traders back; the company's own outlook, which CNBC says expects first-quarter trading volume to fall [[n0679]], says the opposite. When volumes fall, a broker's link to retail enthusiasm works in reverse, and bitcoin's 7.63% slide over 20 sessions from $41,500.88 (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-24) suggests that enthusiasm is already thinner. A bitcoin bounce that fails to revive trading would confirm a crowd that is watching rather than playing.
